title: Determine whether each of the following is a proposition. If it is a proposition, state whether it is True or False. (a) Every prime number greater than 2 is odd. (b) 7 + 8 = 16. (c) The Moon is a planet. (d) India is located in Asia.

title: Define the following terms with examples. (a) Tautology (b) Conditional Statement
answer_html:
(a) Tautology: A compound proposition that is always true, regardless of the truth values of the propositional variables that occur in it. Example: p ∨ ¬p (Either it is raining or it is not raining).

(b) Conditional Statement: A statement of the form p → q, which is false only when p is true and q is false. It is read as 'if p, then q'. Example: If it rains, then I will stay at home.

title: State the converse, contrapositive, and inverse of each of these conditional statements. When I stay up late, it is necessary that I sleep until noon

title: Using logical laws (without truth tables), prove the following (a) (p → q) ≡ (¬q → ¬p) (b) ¬(p → q) ≡ p ∧ ¬q
answer_html:
(a) Prove: (p → q) ≡ (¬q → ¬p)
LHS = p → q
≡ ¬p ∨ q (Implication law)
≡ q ∨ ¬p (Commutative law)
≡ ¬(¬q) ∨ ¬p (Double negation)
≡ ¬q → ¬p (Implication law) = RHS. Hence Proved.

(b) Prove: ¬(p → q) ≡ p ∧ ¬q
LHS = ¬(p → q)
≡ ¬(¬p ∨ q) (Implication law)
≡ ¬(¬p) ∧ ¬q (De Morgan's law)
≡ p ∧ ¬q (Double negation) = RHS. Hence Proved.

title: Let p, q, and r be the propositions p: You have the flu. q: You miss the final examination. r: You pass the course. Express each of these propositions as an English sentence. (a) q → ¬r (b) ¬q ↔ r (c) p ∨ q ∨ r (d) (p → ¬r) ∨ (q → ¬r) (e) (p ∧ q) ∨ (¬q ∧ r)
answer_html:
(a) q → ¬r: If you miss the final examination, then you do not pass the course.

(b) ¬q ↔ r: You do not miss the final examination if and only if you pass the course.

(c) p ∨ q ∨ r: You have the flu, or you miss the final examination, or you pass the course.

(d) (p → ¬r) ∨ (q → ¬r): If you have the flu, then you do not pass the course, or if you miss the final examination, then you do not pass the course.

title: State the converse, contrapositive, and inverse of each of these conditional statements. (a) If it snows tonight, then I will stay at home. (b) I go to the beach whenever it is a sunny summer day.
answer_html:
(a) If it snows tonight, then I will stay at home.

Let p: It snows tonight, q: I stay at home.

Converse (q → p): If I stay at home, then it snows tonight.

Inverse (¬p → ¬q): If it does not snow tonight, then I will not stay at home.

Contrapositive (¬q → ¬p): If I do not stay at home, then it does not snow tonight.

(b) I go to the beach whenever it is a sunny summer day.

This means: If it is a sunny summer day, then I go to the beach. (p: It is a sunny summer day, q: I go to the beach)

Converse: If I go to the beach, then it is a sunny summer day.

Inverse: If it is not a sunny summer day, then I do not go to the beach.

Contrapositive: If I do not go to the beach, then it is not a sunny summer day.

title: Show that ¬(p ∨ (¬p ∧ q)) and ¬p ∧ ¬q are logically equivalent by developing a series of logical equivalences.
answer_html:
We start with the LHS:

¬(p ∨ (¬p ∧ q))

≡ ¬p ∧ ¬(¬p ∧ q) (De Morgan's law)

≡ ¬p ∧ (¬(¬p) ∨ ¬q) (De Morgan's law)

≡ ¬p ∧ (p ∨ ¬q) (Double negation law)

≡ (¬p ∧ p) ∨ (¬p ∧ ¬q) (Distributive law)

≡ F ∨ (¬p ∧ ¬q) (Negation law)

≡ ¬p ∧ ¬q (Identity law)

This is exactly the RHS. Hence proved.

title: Define the following terms with suitable truth table: (a) Tautology (b) Biconditional Statement (c) Contingency (d) Contrapositive (e) Exclusive OR
answer_html:
(a) Tautology: A proposition that is always true. Ex: p ∨ ¬p.

(b) Biconditional Statement: p ↔ q. True when both have same truth value.

(c) Contingency: A proposition that is neither a tautology nor a contradiction (has both True and False values).

(d) Contrapositive: Of p → q is ¬q → ¬p. They are logically equivalent.

(e) Exclusive OR: p ⊕ q. True when exactly one of p or q is true.

(b) F → T is True.

title: Write the characteristic equation corresponding to: a_n - 5a_{n-1} + 6a_{n-2} = 0 and find its complete solution.
answer_html:
The characteristic equation is r^2 - 5r + 6 = 0.

Factoring gives (r - 2)(r - 3) = 0, so the roots are r = 2 and r = 3.

The complete solution is an = c12n + c23n.

answer_html:
The generating function 1 / (1 - rx) corresponds to the sequence r^n.

Here, r = 2, so the solution is an = 2n.

title: Find the number of ways of arranging 3 different books on a shelf from total 5 books?
answer_html:
This is a permutation problem since the order of arrangement matters.

Number of ways = 5P3 = 5! / (5 - 3)! = 5! / 2! = 5 × 4 × 3 = 60.

answer_html:
(a) an = an-1 + an-5 is a linear homogeneous recurrence relation with constant coefficients. Its degree is 5.

(b) an = an-13 + an-2 + n is not linear (due to the cube) and not homogeneous (due to the +n term).

title: Find the value of: (i) 7P2 and (ii) 9C2
answer_html:
(i) 7P2 = 7! / (7-2)! = 7 × 6 = 42.

(ii) 9C2 = 9! / (2! × (9-2)!) = (9 × 8) / 2 = 36.

title: Find the number of ways to select 3 students from a group of 8 students.
answer_html:
This is a combination problem since the order of selection does not matter.

Number of ways = 8C3 = 8! / (3! × 5!) = (8 × 7 × 6) / 6 = 56.

title: Find the generating function for the sequence: 1,2,3,4, ...
answer_html:
The generating function for the constant sequence 1, 1, 1, ... is 1 / (1-x).

Differentiating with respect to x gives the sequence 1, 2, 3, ..., so the generating function is 1 / (1-x)2.

title: Solve the following recurrence relation: a_n = 4a_{n-1} - a_{n-2}
answer_html:
The characteristic equation is r^2 - 4r + 1 = 0.

Using the quadratic formula, the roots are r = (4 ± √12) / 2 = 2 ± √3.

The solution is an = c1(2 + √3)n + c2(2 - √3)n.

title: Check the following terms are the solution of given recurrence relation or not:
answer_html:
(i) Substitute an = n2 into 2an-1 - an-2 + 2:
2(n-1)2 - (n-2)2 + 2 = 2(n2 - 2n + 1) - (n2 - 4n + 4) + 2 = n2 = an. Yes, it is a solution.

(ii) Substitute an = 2n + 1 into 2an-1 - 1:
2(2n-1 + 1) - 1 = 2n + 2 - 1 = 2n + 1 = an. Yes, it is a solution.

title: Solve the following recurrence relation: a_n = 10a_{n-1} - 25a_{n-2}, a_0 = 3, a_1 = 25
answer_html:
Characteristic equation: r^2 - 10r + 25 = 0 ⇒ (r - 5)^2 = 0, so r = 5 (repeated).

General solution: an = (c1 + c2n)5n.

For n=0: 3 = c1.

For n=1: 25 = (3 + c2) × 5 ⇒ 3 + c2 = 5 ⇒ c2 = 2.

Solution: an = (3 + 2n)5n.

title: A committee of 4 students is to be selected from 6 boys and 5 girls. In how many ways can the committee be formed?
answer_html:
Total students = 6 boys + 5 girls = 11.

We need to select a committee of 4 from 11.

Number of ways = 11C4 = 11! / (4! × 7!) = (11 × 10 × 9 × 8) / (4 × 3 × 2 × 1) = 330 ways.

title: Solve the following recurrence relation by using generating function: a_n = 7a_{n-1}, a_0 = -2
answer_html:
Multiply by x^n and sum for n ≥ 1: Σ anxn = 7x Σ an-1xn-1.

Let G(x) be the generating function. Then G(x) - a0 = 7xG(x).

G(x) (1 - 7x) = -2 ⇒ G(x) = -2 / (1 - 7x).

The coefficient of x^n in G(x) gives the sequence: an = -2 × 7n.

title: How many different 4-letter words can be formed using the letters of the word MATH, when each letter can be used only once?
answer_html:
The word MATH has 4 distinct letters.

The number of 4-letter words that can be formed is the number of permutations of 4 letters, which is 4! = 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 24.

title: Solve the following recurrence relation: a_n = 6a_{n-1} - 9a_{n-2}, a_0 = 1, a_1 = 9
answer_html:
Characteristic equation: r^2 - 6r + 9 = 0 ⇒ (r - 3)^2 = 0. Root: r = 3 (repeated).

General solution: an = (c1 + c2n)3n.

For n=0: c1 = 1.

For n=1: (1 + c2)3 = 9 ⇒ 1 + c2 = 3 ⇒ c2 = 2.

Solution: an = (1 + 2n)3n.

title: Solve the following recurrence relation: a_n - 4a_{n-1} + 5a_{n-2} - 2a_{n-3} = 0 given a_0 = 1, a_1 = 3, a_2 = 8
answer_html:
Characteristic equation: r^3 - 4r^2 + 5r - 2 = 0.

Factoring gives (r - 1)^2(r - 2) = 0, so roots are r = 1, 1, 2.

General solution: an = c1 + c2n + c32n.

From conditions:
c1 + c3 = 1
c1 + c2 + 2c3 = 3
c1 + 2c2 + 4c3 = 8.

Solving yields c1 = -2, c2 = -1, c3 = 3.

Solution: an = -2 - n + 3(2n).

title: Solve the following recurrence relation: a_n - 6a_{n-1} + 11a_{n-2} - 6a_{n-3} = 0, given a_0 = 1, a_1 = 6, a_2 = 20
answer_html:
Characteristic equation: r^3 - 6r^2 + 11r - 6 = 0.

Factoring gives (r - 1)(r - 2)(r - 3) = 0, so roots are 1, 2, 3.

General solution: an = c1 + c22n + c33n.

From conditions:
c1 + c2 + c3 = 1
c1 + 2c2 + 3c3 = 6
c1 + 4c2 + 9c3 = 20.

Solving yields c1 = 2, c2 = -3, c3 = 2.

Solution: an = 2 - 3(2n) + 2(3n).

title: Solve the following recurrence relation by using generating function: a_n = 3a_{n-1} + 2a_{n-2} given a_0 = 1, a_1 = 3
answer_html:
Let G(x) be the generating function. Multiply by x^n and sum:
G(x) - 1 - 3x = 3x(G(x) - 1) + 2x^2 G(x).

G(x)(1 - 3x - 2x^2) = 1 ⇒ G(x) = 1 / (1 - 3x - 2x^2).

Let the roots of 1 - 3x - 2x^2 = 0 be finding roots of r^2 - 3r - 2 = 0, r = (3 ± √17)/2.

The sequence is given by expanding via partial fractions, resulting in an = c1((3 + √17)/2)n + c2((3 - √17)/2)n where constants are found from initial conditions.

title: Find the value of n: (n + 1)P_3 = 5 x nP_2
answer_html:
Using the permutation formula: (n+1)! / (n+1-3)! = 5 × [n! / (n-2)!].

(n+1)! / (n-2)! = 5 × n! / (n-2)!

Canceling (n-2)! from both sides gives (n+1)! = 5 × n!.

(n+1)n! = 5n! ⇒ n + 1 = 5 ⇒ n = 4.

title: Solve the following recurrence relation by using generating function: a_n = 3a_{n-1} - 2a_{n-2} given a_0 = 2, a_1 = 5
answer_html:
Let G(x) be the generating function. G(x) - 2 - 5x = 3x(G(x) - 2) - 2x^2 G(x).

G(x)(1 - 3x + 2x^2) = 2 - x ⇒ G(x) = (2 - x) / ((1 - x)(1 - 2x)).

Using partial fractions: (2 - x) / ((1 - x)(1 - 2x)) = A / (1 - x) + B / (1 - 2x).

Solving gives A = -1 and B = 3. Thus, G(x) = -1/(1 - x) + 3/(1 - 2x).

Solution: an = 3(2n) - 1.

title: Solve the following recurrence relation: a_{n+2} - 7a_{n+1} + 12a_n = 0, given a_1 = 2, a_2 = 7.
answer_html:
Characteristic equation: r^2 - 7r + 12 = 0 ⇒ (r - 3)(r - 4) = 0. Roots: 3, 4.

General solution: an = c13n + c24n.

Using conditions: 3c1 + 4c2 = 2 and 9c1 + 16c2 = 7.

Multiply first by 4: 12c1 + 16c2 = 8. Subtracting the second gives 3c1 = 1 ⇒ c1 = 1/3.

Then 4c2 = 2 - 1 = 1 ⇒ c2 = 1/4.

Solution: an = 3n-1 + 4n-1.

title: Solve the following recurrence relation: a_n - 5a_{n-1} + 7a_{n-2} - 3a_{n-3} = 0; a_0 = 2, a_1 = 5, a_2 = 12
answer_html:
Characteristic equation: r^3 - 5r^2 + 7r - 3 = 0. Roots: 1, 1, 3.

General solution: an = c1 + c2n + c33n.

Solving conditions: c1 + c3 = 2, c1 + c2 + 3c3 = 5, c1 + 2c2 + 9c3 = 12.

We get c1 = 1, c2 = 1, c3 = 1.

Solution: an = 1 + n + 3n.

title: Solve the following recurrence relation: a_{n+3} - 5a_{n+2} + 8a_{n+1} - 4a_n = 0, given a_1 = 2, a_2 = 5, a_3 = 14
answer_html:

General solution: an = c1 + (c2 + c3n)2n.

Solving with conditions gives c1 = 5, c2 = -3, c3 = 1.5.

Solution: an = 5 + (-3 + 1.5n)2n.

title: Solve the following recurrence relation: a_n = 11a_{n-1} - 38a_{n-2} + 40a_{n-3}, subject to a_0 = 3, a_1 = 9, a_2 = 27.

General solution: an = c12n + c24n + c35n.

Using conditions, solving 3 equations gives the constants for the exact solution.

title: Solve the following recurrence relation by using generating function: a_n = 2a_{n-1} + 3a_{n-2} given a_0 = 1, a_1 = 2
answer_html:
Let G(x) be the generating function. G(x) - 1 - 2x = 2x(G(x) - 1) + 3x^2 G(x).

G(x)(1 - 2x - 3x^2) = 1 ⇒ G(x) = 1 / ((1 - 3x)(1 + x)).

Using partial fractions: 1 / ((1 - 3x)(1 + x)) = A / (1 - 3x) + B / (1 + x) gives A = 3/4, B = 1/4.

Solution: an = (3/4)3n + (1/4)(-1)n.

title: Solve the following recurrence relation: a_{n+3} - 5a_{n+2} + 8a_{n+1} - 4a_n = 0 given a_1 = 1, a_2 = 4, a_3 = 11
answer_html:

General solution: an = c1 + (c2 + c3n)2n.

Applying conditions a1 = 1, a2 = 4, a3 = 11 allows us to solve for constants c1, c2, c3.

title: Solve the following recurrence relation: a_n = 8a_{n-1} - 21a_{n-2} + 18a_{n-3}, subject to a_0 = 1, a_1 = 5, a_2 = 19.
answer_html:
Characteristic equation: r^3 - 8r^2 + 21r - 18 = 0. Roots: 2, 3, 3.

General solution: an = c12n + (c2 + c3n)3n.

Conditions: c1 + c2 = 1, 2c1 + 3(c2 + c3) = 5, 4c1 + 9(c2 + 2c3) = 19. Solving gives constants c1, c2, c3.

title: Solve the following recurrence relation by using generating function: a_n = a_{n-1} + a_{n-2} given a_0 = 0, a_1 = 1
answer_html:
This is the Fibonacci sequence.

Let G(x) be the generating function. G(x) - x = x G(x) + x^2 G(x).

G(x)(1 - x - x^2) = x ⇒ G(x) = x / (1 - x - x^2).

Using partial fractions with roots of 1 - x - x^2 = 0, we get Binet's formula: an = (1/√5) [ ((1+√5)/2)n - ((1-√5)/2)n ].

title: Define the following terms with graphs: (i) Complete Bipartite Graph (ii) Complete graph
answer_html:
(i) Complete Bipartite Graph: A bipartite graph $G=(V, E)$ with partition $V = V_1 \cup V_2$ is a complete bipartite graph if every vertex in $V_1$ is connected to every vertex in $V_2$. Denoted as $K_{m,n}$.

(ii) Complete graph: A simple graph in which every pair of distinct vertices is connected by a unique edge. Denoted as $K_n$.

title: State the Handshaking Theorem.
answer_html: The Handshaking Theorem states that in any undirected graph, the sum of the degrees of all vertices is equal to twice the number of edges. Mathematically, $\sum_{v \in V} deg(v) = 2|E|$.

title: A graph has 6 vertices with degrees 3, 3, 4, 2, 2, 2. Verify whether such a graph can exist, and if it does, find the total number of edges.
answer_html:

Sum of degrees = $3 + 3 + 4 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 16$.

Since the sum is even, such a graph can exist.

Total number of edges $|E| = 16 / 2 = 8$.

title: (a) A graph has 15 edges. It has one vertex of degree 6, two vertices of degree 5 each, and three vertices of degree 4 each. All remaining vertices have degree 1. Find the total number of vertices in the graph. (b) A graph has 6 vertices with degrees 2,3,4,2,5,x. If the graph has 10 edges, find x.
answer_html:
(a) Total edges $|E| = 15$. Sum of degrees = $2 \times 15 = 30$.

Sum = $6 + 2(5) + 3(4) + k(1) = 28 + k$.

$28 + k = 30 \implies k = 2$. Total vertices = $1 + 2 + 3 + 2 = 8$.

(b) Total edges $|E| = 10$. Sum of degrees = 20.

$2+3+4+2+5+x = 16+x$.

$16+x = 20 \implies x = 4$.
